draft.preheader: Anthropic files for a $2T IPO, Goldman plans its next CEO, and your 2-minute startup question.

lead.headline: Anthropic's IPO filing asks for a $2 trillion valuation
lead.body: Anthropic, the company behind Claude, is heading for a Nasdaq listing, and its prospectus (the S-1) is out. Revenue is exploding, but so is spending: the company plans to put $518 billion into cloud and data centers.

figures.label: of revenue from just two customers

lead.why: Every IPO filing lists its risks. Two customers bringing in a quarter of revenue is called customer concentration, and it's one of the first things a consultant or investor checks. Lose one of those clients and the story changes fast.
sources: Anthropic's $2 trillion IPO prospectus shows steep losses
Stocks edge lower despite $2 trillion Anthropic valuation

stories.headline: Goldman Sachs starts planning for its next CEO
stories.body: COO John Waldron is the leading candidate to succeed David Solomon, who would stay on as executive chairman for a year or two before leaving.
stories.why: Succession at a top bank shapes strategy for a decade. Notice the path: Waldron ran operations before getting the top job.
sources: Goldman Sachs plans CEO succession with John Waldron

stories.headline: Oura delays its IPO even though it's profitable
stories.body: The smart-ring maker has $1.21 billion in sales so far this year and makes money, but pushed back its Nasdaq debut, citing uncertainty in the IPO market.
stories.why: Going public is about timing as much as quality. A strong company can still wait if investors are nervous.
sources: Oura delays IPO amid market uncertainty

stories.headline: AMD buys Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2 billion
stories.body: The chipmaker is buying the spatial-intelligence startup, and Li becomes AMD's chief scientist. The deal should close by year-end if regulators approve.
stories.why: Big companies often buy talent and technology instead of building it. This is an "acqui-hire" at a very large scale.
sources: AMD to acquire Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2 billion

stories.headline: OpenAI holds back a new model over safety concerns
stories.body: OpenAI postponed its next model, citing "alignment" problems, including whether the model accurately reports its own actions.
stories.why: AI companies are now delaying revenue to manage risk. Safety is becoming a business decision, not only a research one.
sources: OpenAI postpones new model over alignment concerns

stories.headline: Summer 2027 internship recruiting is already moving
stories.body: Banks started posting roles as early as December 2025, and the average finance posting draws about 273 applications. Big tech posts in the fall; startups hire mostly in spring.
stories.why: As a freshman you're not expected to land one of these yet. What you can do now: pick five firms you're curious about and follow their careers pages.
sources: The summer 2027 internship race already started

stories.headline: At McKinsey, AI now builds the slides
stories.body: About 75% of McKinsey staff use its internal AI tool, Lilli, which drafts presentations and charts. The firm says it saved 1.5 million hours of work in a year.
stories.why: Junior consulting work is shifting from making decks to judgment and client skills. Those are the skills to build in college.
sources: McKinsey consultants let AI build their slides

stories.headline: UCI ranks 8th among U.S. public universities
stories.body: U.S. News placed UCI in the public top 10 for the 12th year running, and 34th among all national universities.
sources: UC Irvine places eighth among nation's best public universities

stories.headline: Team Europe takes back the Laver Cup, 13–5
stories.body: Alexander Zverev clinched it in London by beating Learner Tien 7-6(3), 6-3.
sources: Team Europe wins Laver Cup 13-5 at The O2

term.name: Shiller CAPE ratio
term.definition: The stock price compared with 10 years of average earnings, adjusted for inflation. A high number means stocks are expensive relative to what companies have actually earned. It's now at levels not seen since 1999, right before the dot-com crash, which is why some analysts are warning about a downturn.
sources: Stocks edge lower despite $2 trillion Anthropic valuation

serve.headline: Atomic raised $12.5M to fix inventory planning
serve.body: Atomic, a Boston startup, uses AI to help supply-chain teams decide how much stock to hold, a job many still run in spreadsheets. Madrona and Klass Capital led the Series A.
